title: XCT Instrument Detail
description: X-ray Computed Tomography images with detailed scan parameters. (Extension type, not in v3 source schema.)

ada:xrayEnergy.description: Accelerating energy of the X-ray source. This block did not declare it at all, while 257 XCTImageCollection subjects carry it -- with its unit in a SEPARATE ada:energyUnit key. Emitted as a QuantitativeValue the two fold into one node, which is why ada:energyUnit is not declared beside it; the block is open, so a record still carrying the split pair is not rejected.

QuantitativeValue.title: Quantitative value with its unit
QuantitativeValue.description:
A measured value carrying its unit, for the XCT parameters that ADA stores BOTH ways. Of the ~700 XCTImageCollection subjects, roughly 360 hold each of these as text with the unit inside it ("90 kV", "11.50844 mm", "33 uA") and roughly 76 as a bare number, so about 2,212 values could not be emitted at all without discarding the unit.
DEFINED HERE rather than reused, after looking. The SHAPE is settled and consistent across five places -- BaseSchema/image, BaseSchema/files, STEM/detail, and CDIF's cdifManifest and dataDownload -- but none of them offers a general reusable $def: image/schema.yaml#/$defs/PixelDimension is the only named one and it types schema:value as an INTEGER for pixel counts, which rejects 11.50844. CDIF's is number-valued but inline. So this is a local $def with one consumer. If a second block needs it, promote it to a shared one rather than copying -- which is the argument PixelDimension's own description already makes, having been written after two blocks declared one property two ways.
IF/THEN/ELSE RATHER THAN ANYOF, and the reason is diagnostics, not taste. Both admit the same two forms, but an anyOf collapses every failure to "is not valid under any of the given schemas" naming no property -- measured. With if/then an object missing its number reports 'schema:value' is a required property, and a value still stored as the text "90 kV" reports is not of type 'number' instead. That matters twice: the counterexample can assert the real cause, and ADA sees a message that says what to fix. It also follows this repo's standing preference for if/then over a narrowed anyOf.
schema:value AND schema:unitText are both REQUIRED. The whole purpose of this branch is to carry the unit, so a QuantitativeValue missing either is not a weaker statement of the same fact, it is a malformed one -- and the plain-number branch is already there for a value with no unit. docs/counterexamples.json pins the schema:value half.
"N/A mm" IS NOT EXPRESSIBLE HERE, deliberately. It appears among the stored values and has a unit but no measurement, so it is an ABSENT reading rather than a quantity. Omit the property instead; the only required property of this block is ada:componentType. Encoding it as a unit-only QuantitativeValue would assert that something was measured in millimetres when nothing was.
schema:unitCode is OPTIONAL and unused today. Allowed because schema.org defines it for exactly this, and it lets ADA add a QUDT or UCUM code later without a schema change; not required, because none of the 2,212 stored values carries one and requiring it would reject every record.
